evidence.disease: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations
evidence.evidence_statement: In this 2017 study, the authors analyzed 91 pediatric B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients and an additional 122 classified as "B-others" lacking conventional genetic abnormalities. ZNF384 rearrangements were identified through whole transcriptome sequencing and PCR-based fusion detection. ZNF384-related fusions were detected in 4.1% of all BCP-ALL cases (9.2% of B-others), with TCF3::ZNF384 being most frequent (2.4% overall). The leukemic cells exhibited a characteristic immunophenotype of weak/absent CD10 and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression, distinct from ZNF384-fusion negative cases. Gene expression profiling revealed enrichment of hematopoietic stem cell features in TCF3::ZNF384 cases, differing from TCF3-PBX1-positive ALL. Clinically, TCF3-ZNF384 patients presented with higher leukocyte counts and poorer steroid response compared to EP300-ZNF384 cases, suggesting fusion partner-dependent heterogeneity. The study demonstrates that ZNF384 rearrangements define a molecularly distinct BCP-ALL subgroup with diagnostic immunophenotypic features, while clinical outcomes vary by fusion partner.

Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor 1 (FGFR1) amplification is frequently observed in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer and is associated with poor prognosis and resistance to endocrine therapy. FGFR inhibitors have shown potential to overcome this resistance. A phase II study, the NCI-MATCH ECOG-ACRIN Trial (EAY131) Subprotocol K1 (NCT06308822), was an open-label, single-arm trial that required central confirmation of FGFR1–4 amplification in tumors. A total of 18 patients were enrolled, including 9 with breast cancer. FGFR amplifications were detected by the NCI-MATCH sequencing assay, with a minimum laboratory reported copy number of 7.0. All participants received oral erdafitinib at a starting dose of 8 mg once daily, with dose escalation to 9 mg permitted based on tolerability. The primary endpoint was the centrally assessed objective response rate (ORR). Key secondary endpoints included 6-month progression-free survival (PFS6), overall PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. No confirmed responses to erdafitinib were observed. However, five patients achieved stable disease as their best response. Notably, one patient with FGFR1-amplified breast cancer experienced prolonged survival, with a PFS exceeding 168 days (5.5 months).

evidence.evidence_statement: In this study, the authors used long-distance inverse PCR and sequencing to comprehensively analyze KMT2A (MLL) gene rearrangements in 2,345 acute leukemia patients, including those with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). The findings reinforce the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-ALL, particularly in infants and young children. The study identified 135 distinct KMT2A rearrangements involving 94 translocation partner genes (TPGs); of those, only 9 fusions accounted for over 90% of the cases, including KMT2A::AFF1, KMT2A::MLLT1, and KMT2A::MLLT3. Among B-ALL patients, the KMT2A::AFF1 (AF4) fusion was the most frequent, especially in infants, followed by KMT2A::MLLT1 (ENL) and KMT2A::MLLT3 (AF9). Importantly, the study highlighted an age-dependent breakpoint shift within the KMT2A locus, with intron 11 breakpoints associated more frequently with B-ALL in younger patients, and intron 9 breakpoints found more often in AML and older patients. This study supports the classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity independent of the fusion partner; this is recognized in the WHO 5th edition (2022) and the International Consensus Classification.

In this publication, the authors conducted a comprehensive genomic analysis of 2,754 pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases using integrated whole genome, exome, and transcriptome sequencing. Of the 2,288 B-ALL cases analyzed, KMT2A rearrangements were identified in approximately 4.5%, confirming their role as a recurrent driver in pediatric B-ALL. These KMT2A-rearranged cases were characterized by a low somatic mutational burden, distinct gene expression profiles, and unique biological features compared to other B-ALL subtypes. The study revealed multiple KMT2A fusion partners, with recurrent fusions involving genes such as MLLT1, MLLT3, AFF1, and others, reinforcing that the diagnostic significance lies in the presence of the KMT2A rearrangement itself, irrespective of the fusion partner. Further sub-classification based on transcriptome clustering identified two transcriptionally distinct KMT2A subgroups—one enriched for NFATC4 expression and the other for CEBPA/FLT3 expression—suggesting underlying differences in developmental origin and potential clinical implications. These findings support the recognition of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity, consistent with the updated 2022 International Consensus Classification (ICC) and the 2024 World Health Organization (WHO) classification.

In this publication, the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) is explored. The study reveals that KMT2A fusions are not restricted to lymphoid lineages but may also involve myeloid compartments and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs), supporting a multilineage origin in a substantial proportion of cases. Notably, 36% of patients with KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL exhibited evidence of multilineage involvement at diagnosis. This finding has important diagnostic implications, as conventional MRD assessment strategies—relying on flow cytometry or immunoglobulin gene rearrangement—may fail to detect residual disease in cases where leukemic clones persist in non-lymphoid compartments. RNA sequencing data further demonstrate a gene expression profile enriched for HSPC and myeloid programs in these patients, reinforcing the hybrid lineage biology of KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating molecular techniques such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or RNA-based assays to detect KMT2A fusions as key diagnostic markers in this B-ALL subtype.

Dovitinib, a pan-FGFR small molecular inhibitor, has shown activity in pre-clinical models against FGFR-expressing breast cancer model cell lines, as well as as in a single agent in a phase II clinical trial in HR+/HER2- FGFR1 amplified breast cancer patients. Notably, this is among patients with higher levels of FGFR amplification. A phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of dovitinib in combination with fulvestrant in postmenopausal women with HR+, HER2− locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression. FGF pathway amplification was determined using TaqMan assay as described by (André F. et al, 2013). Positive amplification for each FGF pathway marker tested (i.e., FGFR1, FGFR2, or FGF3) was defined as a copy number ≥6. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). However, the study had to be stopped early due to slow accrual of patients with FGF pathway amplification. The overall response rate (assessed at regular radiological assessment) in the dovitinib + fulvestrant arm (n=47) was 27.7%, as compared to 10% in the placebo + fulvestrant arm (n=50), irrespective of the presence of FGF pathway amplification. The FGFR-amplified subgroup (n=31) reached a median PFS of 10.9 months vs 5.5 months in the dovitinib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant arms respectively. The final analysis showed limited benefit, with the authors' recommendation to exercise caution when interpreting the study results (particularly the PFS results), due to a fewer than expected number of PFS events (18 vs 50 planned events), as well as the study's small sample size.

evidence.evidence_statement: The Targeted Agent and Profiling Utilizing Registry (TAPUR) study is a prospective, phase II, basket trial that aims to evaluate the antitumor activity of commercially available targeted therapies prescribed to patients with advanced cancer with actionable targets. In this study, sunitinib is evaluated in patients with breast cancer, with FGFR alterations. Patients eligible for the study include those age 12 years or older, who have BC with an FGFR1/2 amplification or mutation. Definitions of amplification were not prespecified in the protocol because of the variety of genomic tests that could qualify a patient for participating in the study. The primary endpoint was disease control (DC) based on the investigator assessment – this was defined as objective response (OR) or stable disease (SD) of at least 16 weeks duration (SD16+), measured from the initiation of study treatment, as determined by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Secondary endpoints were progression free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), duration of response, duration of SD, and safety. Thirty patients with BC with FGFR1 alterations (amplification = 26, mutation = 1, both amp + mut = 3) were initially enrolled. Due to patient ineligibility and drop out, 27 patients were evaluable for sunitinib efficacy (amp=26, mut=1). With regards to DC, two patients were reported with partial response and four with SD16+ were observed for DC. The DC rate was calculated to be 27% (90% CI, 13 to 100) and OR to be 7% (95% CI, 1 to 24). The median PFS was 9 weeks in the FGFR1 cohort (95% CI, 8 to 16). Given the null hypothesis of a 15% DC rate was not rejected, sunitinib did not meet the study’s thresholds for demonstrating antitumor activity in patients with BC harboring FGFR1 amplifications. The study concludes that sunitinib is not recommended for off-label use in FGFR1-altered BC.

evidence.evidence_statement: PALOMA-3, a phase III, multicenter, double-blind randomized controlled trial enrolled patients with advanced estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer receiving fulvestrant (estrogen receptor antagonist) therapy with either palbociclib (a CDK4/6 inhibitor) (N = 347) or placebo (N = 174). Of the total number of 459 patients, 401 patients had enough DNA in pretreatment plasma samples for a custom targeted sequencing panel to assess for mutations (17 genes), copy number alterations (14 genes), and circulating tumor fraction. The prevalence of copy number alterations was assessed only in samples with more than 10% circulating tumor fraction (N=156). Gain of copy number of FGFR1 was observed in 10% (15/156) as one of the most frequent finding, together with gains of MCL1, CCND1, and MYC. In univariable analysis gains in FGFR1 were associated with poorer progression-free survival (PFS) in both treatment groups [HR=3.40, 95% CI 1.91. to 6.04, log-rank Q<0.001 for the group treated with palbociclib plus fulvestrant, and HR = 3.61, 95% CI = 1.31 to 9.97; log-rank Q=0.047 for the group treated with fulvestrant with placebo]. Since an increased circulating tumor fraction was required to detect copy number changes in plasma and higher circulating tumor fraction was also associated with worse PFS, a multivariable analysis was performed. FGFR1 gain remained statistically significant in the model [HR=2.91, 95% CI 1.61 to 5.25, p<0.001]. The median PFS of patients on palbociclib and fulvestrant with detected FGFR1 gain was 3.9 months vs 12.0 months for those without it. In addition, PFS of patients with FGFR1 gain together with TP53 mutations was at 3.7 months. There was no statistically significant interaction for FGFR1 gain with treatment randomization.

evidence.evidence_statement: This study aimed to determine the amplification rates of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR3 in breast cancer and evaluate their impact on prognosis. In a cohort of 894 breast cancer patients, FGFR1 amplification was present in 6.6% (33/503) of assessable tumors and was enriched in the luminal B-like subtype (69.7% of FGFR1-amplified tumors vs. 32.6% of non-amplified tumors). Due to the very low frequency of FGFR2 (<1%) and FGFR3 (<1%) amplifications, outcome analyses focused only on FGFR1 amplification. The results showed that FGFR1 amplification was associated with a trend toward poorer outcomes, particularly shorter distant metastasis–free survival (DMFS; p=0.04, unadjusted analysis); however, this difference did not reach statistical significance in analysis adjusted for other well-known prognostic factors (P=0.05). No significant effect of FGFR1 amplification was observed on other secondary outcomes, including overall survival (OS) and local recurrence–free survival (LRFS). These findings indicate that FGFR1 amplification is disproportionately associated with luminal B-like breast cancers (luminal B-like enriched), which are typically more aggressive and have higher proliferation rates. The absence of a statistically significant prognostic association in this study is likely due to the small number of FGFR1-amplified cases (n = 33), limiting statistical power.

evidence.disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1
evidence.evidence_statement: In this 2005 study, immunohistochemical staining was used to assess the subcellular localization of NPM in 1,835 paraffin-embedded tumor specimens, including 591 from primary AML patients (ages 15–60), 135 from secondary AML patients, and 980 from hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic neoplasms other than AML. Of the 591 specimens tested, 208 (35.2%) were found to have aberrant cytoplasmic NPM localization (NPMc+), while the remainder displayed normal nuclear localization (NPMc–). Subsequent RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing found 51/52 NPMc+ specimens harbored a NPM1 exon 11 (NM_002520) mutation that results in a distinct C-terminal sequence and is predicted to alter the NPM protein at its C-terminus (referred to in this study as NPM exon 12 mutations). Transfection of NIH-3T3 cells with the NPM1 mutant alleles showed aberrant cytoplasmic localization compared to wild type, demonstrating a causal relationship between NPM1 mutation status and aberrant subcellular localization. NPMc+ was found to be associated with a normal karyotype in approximately 60% of AML patients (142/230, 61.7%). FLT3 internal tandem duplications were found to be twice as frequent in NPMc+ vs. NPMc- specimens, suggesting these mutations may be mechanistically linked. The majority of NPMc+ AML specimens were CD34- (49/52) and had a wide morphologic spectrum, demonstrating multilineage involvement. Finally, the authors investigated the response to induction therapy in 126 patients with AML and a normal karyotype (79 NPMc+, 47 NPMc-) treated according to the GIMEMA LAM99P protocol. AML patients with a normal karyotype and NPMc+ were found to have a relatively good response to induction chemotherapy. The study illustrates that AML cases characterized by NPM1 mutations represent a unique disease subtype with shared morphologic features, immunophenotype and molecular and clinical characteristics.

Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1

evidence.disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1
evidence.evidence_statement: In this 2005 study, the authors investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of NPM1 mutation status in 300 adult patients with AML (16-60 years of age) with normal cytogenetics. The diagnostic bone marrow or peripheral blood sample of these 300 patients were analyzed and included the following: 257 patients with de novo AML, 24 patients with t-AML/s-AML, and 19 patients with no available information. NPM1 exon 11 mutations (referred to in this study as NPM exon 12 mutations) were identified in 145/300 (48%) of the specimens tested, representing the most frequent molecular event that has been identified in AML patients with a normal karyotype to-date. The majority of identified NPM1 mutations resulted in a 4 base pair insertion. Universally all mutations resulted in protein elongation and replacement of the last 7 amino acids in NPM1. Mutation status for FLT3, CEPBA, and MLL were also assessed. FLT3 internal tandem duplications (ITDs) and tyrosine kinase domain mutations (TKDs) were more frequently identified in the NPM1-mutated group (41% and 15% respectively) compared to the NPM1 negative group (25% and 5% respectively). NPM1-mutated/FLT3 ITD-negative mutation status was significantly associated with induction success and arose as a prognostic marker for achievement of complete remission (odds ratio = 2.81, 95% CI = 1.39-5.69). In addition, NPM1-mutated/FLT3 ITD-negative patients had significantly better relapse-free survival and overall survival. In summary, NPM1 mutations were frequent in AML and were associated with specific clinical (favorable outcome) and genetic characteristics (normal cytogenetics and FLT3 mutations).

Amplification of FGFR1 is one molecular alteration associated with hormonal resistance and relapse in breast cancer. Using two different patient data cohorts (H12O - patients diagnosed at Hospital 12 de Octubre [n = 251] and METABRIC [n=98 patients]) with hormone-positive breast cancer (HRPBC), FISH studies demonstrated FGFR1 amplification in 11.8% of H12O patients. This was validated in the METABRIC cohort, where 7.6% of HRPBC demonstrated FGFR1 amplification. Furthermore, both studies found that FGFR1 amplification was more common in luminal B (16.3% H12O, 11.1% METABRIC) versus luminal A (6.6%, 5.5%) subtype. Using the H12O cohort, RNA expression analysis revealed 17% of cases had FGFR1 overexpression. Cumulatively, 24.5% of patients had altered FGFR1 expression as measured by FISH (amplification) and/or RNA expression (overexpression). From the H12O cohort, the median relapse-free survival time for patients with FGFR1-amplification was 9.3 years, which is significantly lower than the median relapse-free survival time for patients with non-FGFR1-amplified breast cancer (11.2 years). From the METABRIC cohort, the median relapse-free survival for patients with FGFR1-amplified breast cancer was 12.2 years, which is lower than patients without the FGFR1-amplication in which the median relapse-free survival was 21.1 years. The discrepancy between the median relapse-free survival rates between the cohorts, might be attributed to the demographic and clinical characteristics of the patients in each cohort, with the patients in the METABRIC being slightly older and having earlier stage breast cancer (T1/T2 and N0/N1 stages) than the H12O cohort. However, in both cohorts, when breast cancer was sub-classified by luminal type A or B, the difference in the relapse-free survival time between FGFR1-amplified and non-amplified was no longer significant. When median relapse-free survival included patients with FGFR1 amplification and/or FGFR1 overexpression, the average relapse free survival was 8.8 years for versus 11.2 from non-amplified/non-overexpressed. This analysis combining amplification and overexpression was not performed on the luminal subtypes. In conclusion, FGFR1 amplification is found in HRPBC, more often in the luminal B subtype, and is associated with worse prognosis in HRPBC, however the prognostic consequences of FGFR1 amplification are lost when HRPBC is classified by luminal subtypes.

profile.name: FGFR1 Amplification
profile.summary: FGFR1 amplifications are the most common aberrations of the FGFR family in cancer. One study reports FGFR1 aberrations in 3.5% of 4,853 patients of which most are FGFR1 amplifications (Helsten et. al., 2016). Preclinically, FGFR1 amplifications have also been shown to confer sensitivity to FGFR1 inhibitors (Weiss et. al., 2010). Clinical studies are currently ongoing (e.g. NCT01004224).

evidence.evidence_statement: In a clinical cohort of patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (n=110), FGFR1 amplification status was determined using FISH analysis (FGFR1/centromere 8 ratio ≥2). Among those receiving endocrine therapy alone, FGFR1 amplification (n=30) was associated with poorer outcomes based on time to progression (TTP) compared to those without FGFR1 amplification (n=80). FGFR1 amplification was not associated with a shorter TTP with chemotherapy, and the shorter TTP with endocrine therapy was not observed when combined with an mTOR inhibitor (everolimus). In patients treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor, those with FGFR1 amplification had a shorter TTP, but the sample size was too small to determine statistical significance. A multivariate analysis supported FGFR1 as an independent predictive variable in shorter TTP with endocrine therapy alone but not when combined with mTOR inhibitors.

evidence.evidence_statement: To determine if there is a causal relationship between hormonal blockade (a frequent treatment for tumors in the adjuvant setting) and FGFR1 amplification/overexpression, this study used two non-FGFR1 amplified (MCF7 and T-47D) and one FGFR1 amplified (HCC1428) cell lines and exposed them to prolonged hormonal deprivation to mimic hormonal blockade treatment. After prolonged hormonal deprivation, all three cell lines developed estrogen-deprivation resistance as well as resistance to the selective estrogen receptor degrader, Fulvestrant, a therapy typically used upon metastatic relapse. The two cell lines that came from non-FGFR1 amplified parental lines had increased FGFR1 mRNA and protein levels after prolonged hormonal deprivation. However, engineered overexpression of FGFR1 in the non-FGFR1 amplified parental cell lines did not confer resistance to estrogen deprivation but did confer resistance to Fulvestrant. Furthermore adding Palbociclib, a CDK4/6 inhibitor frequently used in combination with Fulvestrant, all hormone-resistant FGFR1 amplified or overexpressed cell lines were resistant to the Fulvestrant + Palbociclib combination. However, this resistance was lost after adding Rogaratinib, a pan-FGFR inhibitor, to the Fulvestrant + Palbociclib combination, as shown by drastic growth reduction/no growth in culture, suggesting high sensitivity to this triple combination. To further understand mechanisms of resistance and sensitivity, the amount of Rb phosphorylation, CCND1 protein, and BrdU incorporation were measured in the various treatment conditions, due to their role in cell cycle progression. While fulvestrant or palbociclib result in some reduction in Rb phosphorylation, treatment with a doublet combination of fulvestrant + rogaratinib, or triple combination of Fulvestrant, Palbociclib, and Rogaratinib resulted in suppression of Rb phosphorylation and cell cycle arrest. This suggests that the triple blockade of ER, CDK4/6, and FGFR1 might be an appropriate therapy for FGFR1 altered, hormonal resistant breast cancer.

evidence.evidence_statement: FGFR1 amplification (FGFR1amp) is frequently detected in metastatic breast cancer (MBC), where it is recognized as a generic marker of poor prognosis and most notably, resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors and endocrine therapy. This prompted development of multityrosine kinase inhibitors (MTKIs) and pan-selective FGFR inhibitors (FGFRis) to treat specifically FGFR1-altered breast cancer; however, not all patients with FGFR1amp responded to FGFRis, leading to the hypothesis that FGFR mRNA expression may be a more accurate predictor of treatment response than gene copy number alterations (CNAs). In addition, up to 30% of breast cancers reveal concurrent amplification of FGFR1 and amplification of 11q13 segment encompassing cyclin D1 (CCND1) and 3 FGF ligands (FGFR3/4/19). Thus, 17 breast cancer patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) harboring amplifications in FGFR1 or 4 and/or 11q13 amplification (7 PDXs and FGFR1amp without 11q13amp, 4 PDXs with co-amplification of FGFR1 and 11q13, 3 PDXs with FGFR4amp, and 3 PDXs with 11q13amp), and samples from 10 patients treated with either FGFRis or MTKIs, were evaluated for antitumor activity. FFPE tumor samples were used for mRNA levels measurement (using nCounter and HTG EdgeSeq methods), and treatment effects on proliferation and angiogenesis were assessed by immunofluorescence detection of Ki-67 and CD31. High FGFR1–4 mRNA expression, rather than CNAs, was a more accurate biomarker for FGFRi sensitivity, with responders showing MAPK pathway downregulation. Rogaratinib, a pan-FGFR1–4 inhibitor, achieved partial or stable responses in 53% of models, while lucitanib, an MTKI, showed superior efficacy (86%) across FGFRi-resistant and FGFR-independent models due to its dual antiproliferative and antiangiogenic effects. Amplification of the 11q13 locus, which includes FGF3/4/19 and CCND1, frequently co-occurred with FGFR1amp and enhanced FGFRi sensitivity, especially when FGF ligands were overexpressed. A composite biomarker based on FGFR1–4 mRNA levels predicted treatment response with high accuracy (ROC AUC = 0.94), and in a cohort of 339 breast cancer samples, FGFR1 CNA was frequent but only moderately correlated with mRNA expression. Attempts to mimic lucitanib’s dual mechanism by combining rogaratinib with anti-VEGF agents showed limited efficacy, underscoring the therapeutic advantage of MTKIs like lucitanib in FGFR-addicted and resistant breast cancers. In conclusion, FGFR inhibitors may offer effective treatment for metastatic breast cancer patients with high FGFR1–4 mRNA expression, especially those resistant to CDK4/6 inhibitors or lacking targeted options in triple-negative breast cancer, but this approach requires further clinical validation.

In a phase II trial of 49 NSCLC patients with STK11 mutation, the MTORC1/2 inhibitor vistusertib did not result in any responses.

Preclinical studies demonstrated that the LSD1 inhibitor HCI-2509 reduced proliferation and induced apoptosis in five EWSR1-FLI1 fusion-positive Ewing sarcoma cell lines (A673, TC32, TC71, SK-N-MC, CHLA-10) compared to DMSO controls (p < 0.05), whereas non-Ewing sarcoma lines were relatively resistant. In A673 cells, fusion dependence was confirmed as EWSR1-FLI1 fusion (EWS/FLI) knockdown reduced drug sensitivity (EC50 113nM, 95% CI 81.9 - 158nM, 95% CI 1,111 - 2,999). In xenograft models derived from A673, TC71, and SK-N-MC cells (n = 8-10 per arm), daily HCI-2509 treatment significantly delayed tumor growth compared with vehicle (two-way ANOVA P<0.0001) and improved survival (log-rank P<0.05), with histologic evidence of reduced Ki-67 and increased cleaved caspase-3.

profile.name: EWSR1::FLI1 Fusion
profile.summary: In approximately 90% of Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (ES/PNET) a translocation t(11;22)(q24; q12) is identified, fusing the 5’ exons (containing the transactivatin domain, at least exon 1-7) of EWSR1, with the 3’ exons (from exon 9, coding the DNA binding domain) of FLI1.

evidence.evidence_statement: In this 2017 study the author included 44 cellular myofibroblastic tumors previously diagnosed as cellular myofibroma, cellular myopericytoma, or cellular myofibroblastic neoplasms (NOS), and a control group of 34 various myofibroblastic lesions, including typical myofibromas (adult and infantile variants), myopericytomas, malignant myopericytomas, low grade myofibroblastic sarcomas, and myofibroblastomas. RT-PCR and FISH was utilised to investigate SRF gene abnormalities. SRF gene rearrangements were detected in 10 cases of cellular myofibroblastic tumors and not detected in any of the control group, including classic examples of both myofibroma and myopericytoma. SRF::RELA fusions were present in 7 tumours, while another case had a SRF::C3orf62 fusion and in two cases the partner was not identified. RT-PCR confirmed fusion of SRF exon 4 with RELA exon 11 in one case. The cohort was composed of 7 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, of 3 months to 63 years (mean 17; median 14), the majority under the age of 18 years. The anatomic distribution was quite broad. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of cellular myofibroblastic tumors occurring mostly in children and young adults, with morphologic features in keeping with cellular variants of myofibroma and myopericytoma, and harboring recurrent gene rearrangements in the SRF gene which in the majority of these cases resulted in SRF::RELA gene fusions.

In this 2020 study, the authors include 13 perivascular myoid tumors belonging to the previously described SRF rearranged subtype of tumors (PMID:28248815), which share morphologic features with myopericytomas and myofibromas and express smooth muscle markers similarly to most perivascular myoid tumors. The cohort was composed of 6 males and 7 females, and all patients except 1 were pediatric, with a mean age of 11.8 years (ranging from 1 week to 73 years). RNA-sequencing was successfully performed on 12 samples and detected the SRF::RELA fusion in 6 tumors, SRF::NCOA2 in 3 tumors, while SRF::CITED1, SRF::NFKBIE, and CITED2::SRF were detected once. The breakpoints were located in exons (ENST00000265354) 2 to 5 of the SRF gene. The tumors occurred in different anatomic sites, although often tumors (n=8) were situated in the head. Follow-up data showed that tumors seem to be nonaggressive. The authors concluded that they have expanded the molecular spectrum of the perivascular tumors with SRF rearrangement by identifying 4 additional fusion genes and suggest naming the distinct clinicopathologic entity SRF-fused perivascular tumor.

In this 2023 study, the authors included 3 cases of SRF rearranged cellular myofibromas/perivascular myoid tumors diagnosed in children, aged 7 to 16 years. RNA sequencing was utilized to detect SRF::NCOA3, SRF::RELA, and SRF::NFKBIE gene fusions in the 3 tumors. All 3 cases occurred in the extremities. The authors concluded that they have described 3 cases of rare SRF rearranged cellular myofibromas/perivascular myoid tumors with a smooth muscle-like phenotype in children and expanded the molecular spectrum by identifying a new fusion gene, NCOA3.

In this 2024 case report, the authors included 2 cases of SRF rearranged cellular perivascular myoid tumors diagnosed in a 3-month-old male and a 3-year-old female. FISH and next-generation sequencing were utilised to detect an SRF::NCOA2 gene fusion in case 1 and a SRF::RELA gene fusion in case 2, respectively. The authors conclude that SRF rearranged cellular perivascular myoid tumors have a broad morphologic spectrum ranging from a pericytic pattern to a myoid pattern, and include hybrid tumors with a mixture of pericytic and myoid patterns, and can be misdiagnosed as myogenic sarcomas.

In this Swedish population-based study, the authors retrospectively re-evaluated 71 poorly differentiated supratentorial CNS tumors in children, previously diagnosed as CNS-PNETs, to assess their molecular features, including BCOR genetic alterations. The cohort included 39 males and 32 females, with a median age at diagnosis of 6.2 years. Using WHO 2021 histopathological guidelines and the Molecular Neuropathology (MNP) brain tumor classifier, 10% (n=7) of tumors were subclassified as CNS neuroblastoma with FOXR2 activation (CNS NB-FOXR2). All seven CNS NB-FOXR2 tumors showed complete concordance between histology-based diagnoses and DNA methylation-based classification, with a calibrated score (CS) ≥ 0.9. The median age at diagnosis of CNS NB-FOXR2 patients was 5.3 years (range 2.5–15.7), with 43% males (n=3) and 57% females (n=4). Copy number analysis predicted gain of chromosome 1q in all seven tumors, and whole or partial loss of chromosome 16q in 86% (6/7) of cases. While the overall CNS-PNET cohort demonstrated poor outcomes (5-year PFS 38% ±11%, 5-year OS 45% ±12%), CNS NB-FOXR2 patients had excellent prognosis, with both 5-year PFS and OS at 100%. These findings highlight that CNS NB-FOXR2 represents a rare, molecularly distinct entity within pediatric CNS-PNETs, and that DNA methylation profiling provides a reliable diagnostic tool to accurately identify this tumor type, which is associated with favorable long-term outcomes.

Phase II trial (NCT04484142) of Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks in 137 heavily pretreated patients with advanced NSCLC harboring actionable genomic alterations (57% EGFR-mutant; 51% with prior brain metastases). The confirmed ORR was 35.8% (95% CI 27.8–44.4) with a median DOR of 7.0 months. In subgroup analyses, ORR was 43.6% (95% CI 32.9-54.8) in EGFR-mutant patients and 23.5% in those with ALK rearrangements, with corresponding median PFS of 5.8 and 4.3 months. All four complete responses occurred in patients with EGFR mutations. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs occurred in 28.5% of patients, most commonly stomatitis (9.5%), with oral mucositis and anemia as notable AESIs.

TROPION-Lung01 (NCT04656652) was a global, randomized, open-label phase III trial of 604 patients with previously treated advanced NSCLC comparing datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) with docetaxel. Dato-DXd significantly improved progression-free survival (4.4 vs 3.7 months; HR 0.75; P = 0.004) but not overall survival (12.9 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.94; P = 0.530), with greater benefit in nonsquamous disease (PFS HR 0.63; OS HR 0.84) and a higher objective response rate (26.4% vs 12.8%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were less frequent with Dato-DXd (25.6% vs 42.1%), with stomatitis and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as notable adverse events of special interest (AESIs).

In this 2016 study, the authors analyzed 398 newly diagnosed Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) patients, identifying 12 (3%) cases that lacked the Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome by conventional cytogenetic analysis but were positive for the BCR::ABL1 fusion by RT-PCR. Six Ph– cases were further characterized to investigate the cytogenetic mechanisms responsible for this rearrangement. FISH analysis revealed cryptic insertions between chromosomes 9 and 22 in five patients and a classic two-step translocation in one patient, demonstrating four distinct fusion signal patterns and highlighting significant genetic heterogeneity among Ph– CML cases. The study found that the BCR::ABL1 fusion most frequently localized to chromosome 9q34 rather than the typical 22q11.2 region, contrasting with prior reports. These findings established that even in the absence of the visible Philadelphia chromosome, the presence of the BCR::ABL1 fusion gene serves as a definitive diagnostic hallmark of CML. The authors concluded that detection of BCR::ABL1 by FISH or molecular analysis is essential for confirming the diagnosis of CML in patients with a normal karyotype, supporting its role as the primary molecular event defining the disease.

profile.name: BCR::ABL1 Fusion
profile.summary: The BCR-ABL fusion protein, commonly referred to as the Philadelphia chromosome, is one of the most studied fusion genes in cancer. It has widely been considered the initiating event in chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). However, despite its ability to initiate disease in mice, its status as an initiating mutation is in dispute. In what is commonly used as the poster-child for targeted therapeutics, the development and use of imatinib in the clinic has led to profound improvements in the prognosis of the disease. However, imatinib resistance is still seen in patients with mutations in the ABL kinase domain of the fusion, most notably the T315I variant. In patients resistant to imatinib, either acquired or otherwise, second generation BCR-ABL TKI's (dasatinib and nilotinib) have seen some success in delivering a tumor response. Third generation ABL1 inhibitor ponatinib is the only FDA approved drug with activity against T315I . However due to risk of life-threatening blood clots and severe narrowing of blood vessels ponatinib is ONLY approved for T315I-positive CML or T315I-positive Ph+ ALL or in cases of CML, Ph+ ALL with resistance or intolerance to other approved ABL1 inhibitors.

evidence.evidence_statement: The authors report evaluation of zongertinib in a multicohort, phase 1a/1b trial involving patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. Three cohorts of patients are reported. The cohorts differed in the type of ERBB2 mutation present, prior treatment, and in the treatment dose/timing with zongertinib. In cohort 1 (n=75), patients had a mutation in the tyrosine kinase domain of ERBB2, received zongertinib at a dose of 120 mg, and were NOT previously treated with a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate. 71% of these patients (95% [CI], 60 to 80; P<0.001 against a ≤30% benchmark) had a confirmed objective response. The median duration of response was 14.1 months (95% CI, 6.9 to not evaluable). The median progression-free survival was 12.4 months (95% CI, 8.2 to not evaluable).

The phase III INAVO120 trial (NCT04191499) in 325 patients with endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated HR⁺/HER2⁻ locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer evaluated inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant (n=161) versus placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant (n=164). Median PFS was 15.0 months (95% CI 11.3–20.5) versus 7.3 months (95% CI 5.6–9.3; HR 0.43; 95% CI 0.32–0.59; P<.0001), with ORR of 58% (95% CI 50–66) and median DOR of 18.4 months compared to 25% (95% CI 19–32) and 9.6 months in the control arm. The most common adverse events (≥20%) included neutropenia, hyperglycemia, stomatitis, diarrhea, and rash, consistent with the PI3Kα inhibitor class. Efficacy outcomes were reported for all eligible PIK3CA mutations detected by the FoundationOne Liquid CDx assay, which covers hotspot mutations in exons 2 (R88, G106, K111, G118), 5 (N345), 8 (C420, E453), 10 (E542, E545, Q546), and 21 (M1043, H1047, G1049); individual patient numbers by mutation were not provided.

Median PFS was 15.0 months (95% CI 11.3–20.5) versus 7.3 months (95% CI 5.6–9.3; HR 0.43; 95% CI 0.32–0.59; P<.0001), with ORR of 58% (95% CI 50–66) and median DOR of 18.4 months compared to 25% (95% CI 19–32) and 9.6 months in the control arm. The most common adverse events (≥20%) included neutropenia, hyperglycemia, stomatitis, diarrhea, and rash, consistent with the PI3Kα inhibitor class. Efficacy outcomes were reported for all eligible PIK3CA mutations detected by the FoundationOne Liquid CDx assay, which covers hotspot mutations in exons 2 (R88, G106, K111, G118), 5 (N345), 8 (C420, E453), 10 (E542, E545, Q546), and 21 (M1043, H1047, G1049); individual patient numbers by mutation were not provided.

evidence.evidence_statement: The phase 2 FIGHT-207 basket study was designed to evaluate pemigatinib, a selective FGFR inhibitor, in patients with previously treated advanced solid tumors harboring FGFR alterations. Eligible patients were ≥18 years old with a histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced/metastatic or surgically unresectable solid tumor and radiographically measurable disease per RECIST v.1.1 or RANO criteria. Safety was consistent with previous reports. This study consisted of three cohorts defined by FGFR alteration category. Patients with in-frame FGFR1–FGFR3 fusions and rearrangements, including intact kinase domains, were assigned to cohort A (n=49). Cohort B (n=32) consisted of patients with FGFR actionable single-nucleotide variants (SNVs), excluding kinase domain SNVs, considered known or likely to be activating and actionable. This set included specific somatic missense mutations, insertions or deletions of FGFR1–FGFR3 that were known or likely activating. Cohort C (n=26) included the remaining patients with FGFR1–FGFR3 mutations in the kinase domain or FGFR1–3 VUS with potential pathogenicity. Most patients underwent local testing with the FoundationOne CDx assay (Foundation Medicine), which profiles 324 genes at high coverage (>500×), with some tested using alternative platforms. Six Breast Cancer patients were included in this study: One in cohort B and five in cohort C. FGFR amplification, defined as a copy number ≥6, was identified in nine patients. These included cases with concurrent FGFR mutations or fusions, as well as amplifications in alternative FGFR genes unrelated to the primary alteration. FGFR1 amplification was observed in five patients, including two breast cancer cases in cohort C. Exploratory endpoints included objective response rate (ORR) of cohort C and analysis of co-alterations associated with resistance and response. ORRs for cohorts A, B and C were 26.5% (13/49), 9.4% (3/32) and 3.8% (1/26), respectively. Although new therapeutic areas for FGFR inhibition and mechanisms of drug failure were identified across tumor types, the FIGHT-207 study was terminated early by the sponsor for business reasons. As a result, some tumor and molecular cohorts were underpowered, limiting the ability to draw definitive conclusions about FGFR dependency for specific alterations. Additionally, the small number of patients with concurrent FGFR gene amplification precluded evaluation of its potential impact on pemigatinib response.

profile.name: FGFR1 Amplification
profile.summary: FGFR1 amplifications are the most common aberrations of the FGFR family in cancer. One study reports FGFR1 aberrations in 3.5% of 4,853 patients of which most are FGFR1 amplifications (Helsten et. al., 2016). Preclinically, FGFR1 amplifications have also been shown to confer sensitivity to FGFR1 inhibitors (Weiss et. al., 2010). Clinical studies are currently ongoing (e.g. NCT01004224).

In retrospective analyses of two large ICI-treated solid tumor cohorts (DFCI n = 789, MSKCC n = 1250), CDKN2A loss-of-function alterations were associated with significantly worse overall survival and shorter time-to-treatment failure in urothelial carcinoma (UC DFCI n = 109, UC MSKCC n = 206). In the DCFI cohort, median OS was 8.8 vs 25.2 months (HR 1.8, 95% CI 1.1–3.1; p = 0.019) and median TTF 4.2 vs 8.4 months (HR 2.0, 95% CI 1.3–3.1; p = 0.002), while in the MSKCC cohort median OS was 11 vs 19 months (HR 1.7; 95% CI 1.1–2.6; p = 0.017). Futibatinib is a selective FGFR inhibitor. In this 2020 preclinical study, its antitumor activity was evaluated in cancer cell lines and xenograft models. The antiproliferative activity was assessed in cancer cell lines derived from various tissue origins, including the MFM-223 and MDA-MB-134-VI breast cancer cell lines, with or without FGFR genomic aberrations (amplifications, point mutations, fusions, or translocations), by measuring cell growth after three days of futibatinib exposure. Additionally, the antitumor activity of futibatinib was investigated in murine and rat xenograft models bearing tumors with FGFR genomic alterations. Mice received oral doses of futibatinib once daily for two weeks. Futibatinib demonstrated antiproliferative activity against the FGFR-deregulated MFM-223 breast cancer cell line, which harbors FGFR1/2 amplifications. Furthermore, robust tumor growth inhibition was observed in the FGFR1/2-amplified MFM-223 breast cancer xenograft model at daily doses ranging from 12.5 to 50 mg/kg. In summary, the results of this study demonstrate that futibatinib is a potent, irreversible, and highly selective inhibitor of FGFR1–4, exhibiting broad antiproliferative activity in FGFR-deregulated cancer cell lines and animal tumor models.

Loss of STK11 increased expression of PDE4D, PDE4B, and PDE10A, and roflumilast reversed pro-migratory/angiogenic gene signatures. Treatment was well tolerated with no observed toxicity.

In a cell line screen using MCF-7, exogenous expression of FGFR1 confers resistance to fulvestrant and fulvestrant plus ribociclib. In a study using breast cancer cell lines MCF-7 and T47D, overexpression of FGFR1 was found to confer resistance to fulvestrant plus ribociclib. Conversely, inhibition of FGFR signaling in three estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer cell lines with FGFR1 amplification restores sensitivity to fulvestrant/palbociclib combination. Growth of patient derived xenograft models harbouring FGFR1 amplification can be suppressed by the combination of FGFR inhibitor, fulvestrant and palbociclib. These observations are consistent with those of the MONALEESA cohort, where amplification or mRNA overexpression of FGFR1 is associated with shorter PFS when treated with CDK4/6 inhibitor, suggesting that FGFR1 amplification or overexpression is a mechanism of resistance to the combination treatment of fulvestrant and CDK4/6 inhibitor.

In a retrospective study of stage IV NSCLC patients treated with first-line platinum doublet chemotherapy (n = 103; 51 KEAP1/NFE2L2/CUL3-mutant, 52 WT), mutations in NFE2L2, KEAP1, or CUL3 were associated with significantly shorter time to treatment failure (2.8 vs 8.3 months; HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.42–3.38; p = 0.00036) and overall survival (11.2 vs 36.8 months; HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.34–3.52; p = 0.0016) compared with matched controls. In KRAS wild-type cases, OS (11.2 vs 38.1 months; p = 0.0039) and time on treatment (2.6 vs 8.5 months, p = 0.0001) remained shorter when compared to WT patients. Preclinical Keap1-deleted Trp53-based LUAD and LSCC mouse models lacking Kras mutations demonstrated increased clonogenic survival after exposure to cisplatin, carboplatin, paclitaxel, and etoposide, confirming that Keap1 loss drives intrinsic chemoresistance through NRF2 pathway activation.

evidence.evidence_statement: In preclinical pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) models with high NQ01 expression, which indicates the NFE2L2 (NRF2) pathway activation, the small molecule NSC84167 (NSLC01, 50 mg/kg) selectively inhibited tumor growth (p < 0.01, n = 7-8) and induced apoptosis in NRF2-high but not in NRF2-low PDXs. Across conventional and patient-derived PDAC cell lines, NSLC01 sensitivity correlated with NQO1 expression (r = −0.5563, p = 0.021), and NRF2 knockdown reversed drug sensitivity.

In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 303, 255 centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer), nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus investigator’s choice of chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI with or without bevacizumab or cetuximab) as first-line treatment (24-month PFS 72%, 95% CI 64–79 vs 14%, 95% CI 6–25; p < 0.001). The restricted mean survival time at 24 months was 10.6 months longer (95% CI 8.4–12.9) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, and grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 23% vs 48% of patients, respectively.

profile.name: MSI High
profile.summary: High microsatellite instability will often arise in cases where mismatch repair is deficient (dMMR). In tumors with MSI, marker length at microsatellite sequences will differ from that in normal tissue. Determination of MSI-High will usually include criteria such as tumor DNA showing additional microsatellite alleles of different lengths in multiple microsatellite markers, or greater than one third of all microsatellite markers examined. MSI-H has been associated to better prognosis in colorectal cancer, and also reported to be associated with sensitivity to checkpoint inhibition therapy in some instances.

evidence.evidence_statement: In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 707 randomized; centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR: n = 296 nivolumab+ipilimumab vs 286 nivolumab) showed nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus nivolumab monotherapy across all treatment lines (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.81; p = 0.0003). Median PFS was not reached (95% CI 53.8-NE) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 39.3 months (22.1-NE) with nivolumab. Objective response rate was 71% (95% CI 65–76) vs 58% (95% CI 52–64; p = 0.0011), with complete responses in 30% and 28%, respectively. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 22% vs 14%, including diarrhea/colitis (3%), hypophysitis (3%), and adrenal insufficiency (3%), with three treatment-related deaths reported (2 myocarditis/pneumonitis in combination arm, 1 pneumonitis in monotherapy arm).

evidence.evidence_statement: In the multicohort phase 1b Beamion LUNG-1 trial (NCT04886804) of zongertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC, three cohorts were evaluated by mutation type and prior therapy. In cohort 1 (n = 75; HER2-TKD mutations, no prior HER2-ADC), the confirmed ORR was 71% (95% CI 60-80; P < 0.001), with median duration of response 14.1 months (95% CI 6.9-NE) and mPFS 12.4 months (95% CI 8.2-NE). Responses occurred across subtypes, including A775_G776insYVMA 81% (95 % CI 68-90); P780_Y781insGSP 75% (95% CI 41-93); other mutations 42% (95% CI 23-64). AEs included diarrhea (56%) and rash (33%) with grade ≥3 drug-related adverse events occurring in 17% (Alanine aminotransferase 8%, Aspartate aminotransferase 5%), and no treatment-related interstitial lung disease was reported.

In this 2017 study reviewing 753 sarcoma cases, 11 tumors with the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion were identified using immunohistochemistry and RT-PCR. These tumors were found exclusively in males, with a mean age of 12.9 years, and were predominantly located in the axial skeleton. Morphologically, the tumors showed spindled or round cells, vesicular nuclei, fine chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a characteristic arciform vascular pattern. Over 50% stained positive for SATB2 and Pax8, suggesting potential diagnostic value for these markers in identifying BCOR::CCNB3 positive sarcomas.

Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome occurred in 10% and 30% of patients, and all events resolved. These results support the activity of lete-cel for HLA-/NY-ESO-1-positive MRCLS.

Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) colorectal cancers (CRC) respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICPIs), but response rates vary, often < 50%, highlighting the need for better stratification. This retrospective study evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) as a predictive biomarker in 22 MSI-H mCRC patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, including 19 on pembrolizumab. Among these patients, ORR was 68% (15/22), with 7 complete and 8 partial responses. TMB was strongly associated with ORR and PFS in both univariate (P < 0.001) and multivariate (P < 0.01) analyses. Log-rank analysis identified the optimal TMB cut-point between 37 and 41 mutations/Mb. All patients with TMB ≥37 responded; most (6 of 9 ) with lower TMB progressed. Median PFS was not reached in the TMB-high group (median follow-up >18 months), while it was 2 months in the TMB-low group. Validation in a larger cohort of 18,140 CRC cases (821/4.5% MSI-H) confirmed the cut-point (37.4 mutations/Mb), corresponding to the 35th percentile. Patients below this threshold were less likely to benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy. TMB was measured from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue using a hybrid capture-based NGS assay (Foundation Medicine), targeting 315–324 cancer-related genes across a 0.8–1.2 Mb genomic region. The assay used somatic-only sequencing with computational germline filtering. TMB calculations included both synonymous and non-synonymous variants and were validated against whole exome sequencing (WES), ensuring methodological accuracy. These findings support integrating TMB into clinical workflows and highlight the need for prospective validation in larger cohorts.

evidence.evidence_statement: In non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) models, KEAP1-mutant cell lines (H838, H460) exhibited strong sensitivity to NSC84167 (NSLC01) in MTT cell viability assays, with IC₅₀ values well below 1 µM, which is considerably lower than the 3 µM cutoff for sensitivity. In contrast, KEAP1-wild-type cells (HCC193, H1299) were resistant. This pattern suggests that loss of KEAP1 and subsequent NRF2 pathway activation predict a response to NSLC01.

This retrospective study examined the association between TMB and clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) across multiple cancer types. 1,662 advanced cancer patients treated with at least one dose of ICI, including avelumab, durvalumab, ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab or tremelimumab as monotherapy or in combination (146 received anti-CTLA-4, 1,256 received anti-PD-1 or PD-L1, and 260 received the combination), were included in the study. Tumour-derived and matched normal germline DNA were sequenced using the MSK-IMPACT targeted 468-cancer gene panel. TMB was calculated as the number of somatic nonsynonymous per megabase sequences. Using top 20% within each cancer type as the cutoff, a significant association of improved overall survival with higher TMB was observed in patients with bladder (n=214, p=0.040), colorectal (n=110, p= 0.031), head and neck (n=138, p=7.42 × 10e-3), and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (n=350, p= 2.30× 10e-4), and across the whole cohort (n=1,662, p= 1.59 × 10e-6). A similar trend was also observed in breast cancer (n=45), esophagogastric cancer (n=126), melanoma (n=321), renal cell carcinoma (n=151), and cancer of unknown primary (n=90), despite not reaching statistical significance. This association was also observed using different cut points ranging between top10-50% to define high TMB. Similarly, improved clinical benefit/ progression free survival were also associated higher TMB among patients with NSCLC, melanoma, esophagogastric, head and neck, and renal cell carcinoma. Notably, distinct from these cancer types, no association between higher TMB and improved patient survival was observed in glioma (n=117). A cohort of 5,371 advanced cancer patients who did not receive ICI were also included in this study. A lack of prognostic benefit of TMB status was observed both across the cancer types and within each histology, demonstrating the observed survival difference among patients with TMB high tumours was attributed to ICI treatment. The authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use. Overall, this study demonstrated the clinical value of higher TMB in predicting superior overall survival in patients across multiple cancer types. However, the authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.

evidence.evidence_statement: High Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB >19 mutations/Mb) represents a robust and platform-validated genomic biomarker predictive of clinical benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This threshold was derived through regression tree modeling across multiple sequencing platforms (MSK-IMPACT, DFCI-OncoPanel, and whole-exome sequencing) and validated in three large, independent cohorts totaling 1,552 patients. Patients with high TMB demonstrated significantly improved objective response rate (49.1% vs 21.5%, p<0.001), progression-free survival (11.4 vs 2.8 months, p<0.001), and overall survival (36.1 vs 12.4 months, p<0.001) compared with those with low TMB, independent of PD-L1 expression levels. Molecular and immune profiling revealed that high-TMB NSCLCs exhibit enhanced CD8⁺ and PD-1⁺ T-cell infiltration, increased PD-L1 expression, and activation of antigen presentation pathways. The authors suggested that TMB >19 mut/Mb is a clinically actionable biomarker for identifying NSCLC patients most likely to respond to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

evidence.evidence_statement: This retrospective study evaluated the clinical utility of blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for atezolizumab efficacy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had progressed from first-line therapy using samples collected prospectively from 2 randomized trials. The cfDNA assay used in this study utilised the same 1.1 Mb tissue FoundationOne hybridization capture panel (394 genes). The bTMB score was calculated by identifying all base substitutions present at an allele frequency of ≥0.5%, with predicted germline variants filtered out. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.64, n=259). Based on this correlation, an optimal cut-off point of ≥ 16 mutations per megabase (with a minimum somatic allele frequency ≥ 1%) was selected for subsequent clinical evaluation. The median PFS was 4.2 months in the atezolizumab arm and 2.9 months in the docetaxel arm; the median OS values were 13.0 and 7.4 months, respectively. evidence.evidence_statement: This retrospective analysis assessed the association between tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the efficacy of nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab as first-line treatment for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the CheckMate 568 trial (NCT02477826). The TMB was calculated using the FoundationOne CDx assay, which covers 324 genes. TMB was defined as the number of somatic, coding, base substitutions, and short indels per Mb of genome examined, with predicted germline variants excluded from the calculation. Of the 139 patients enrolled, 98 had successful TMB results, where 49% of patients had high-TMB (defined as ≥ 10 mut/Mb). The overall response rate (ORR) was 44% in the high-TMB group versus 12% in the low-TMB group. The association of efficacy with TMB was independent of tumor PD-L1 expression status. TMB was shown to be an informative classifier for ORR (AUC= 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was also longer in patients with high-TMB compared to those with low-TMB (7.1 months [95% CI, 3.6 to 11.3 months] and 2.6 months [95% CI, 1.4 to 5.4 months], respectively). At 6 months, 55% of the high-TMB subgroup remained progression-free vs 31% in the low-TMB subgroup. The cut-off of 10 mut/Mb was selected for this retrospective analysis as the ORR exceeded 40% which was higher than historical chemotherapy responses, and a higher TMB cutoff did not result in additional improvement. Further prospective validation in a larger randomized study is required to validate this selected cut-off and its predicative effect for nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab in NSCLC.

evidence.evidence_statement: In this 2009 study, the authors included 336 chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients at diagnosis, of which 25 patients (7.44%) exhibited variant Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome translocations. A control group of patients with the standard t(9;22) translocation was used for comparison. Conventional cytogenetics and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) were utilized to characterize the variant translocations and investigate deletions on the derivative chromosome 9 [der(9)]. Variant Ph translocations, involving chromosomes 9, 22, and one or more additional chromosomes, were identified in all 25 cases. The BCR::ABL1 fusion gene was detected in all patients, confirming the diagnosis of CML despite the complex karyotypes. Deletions adjacent to the ABL1 gene on der(9) were observed in 15 of the 25 cases (60%), a significantly greater proportion than that found in typical Ph translocations (12–15%). The genesis of these variants was attributed to both one-step (36%) and two-step (56%) mechanisms, with the latter being more prevalent. The cohort was composed of patients where any chromosome could be involved, with breakpoints preferentially located in the CG-richest regions of the genome. The authors concluded that the BCR::ABL1 fusion is the fundamental diagnostic event in CML, even in cases with complex variant translocations. They identified that these variant translocations are associated with a markedly higher incidence of deletions on der(9). Proper assessment of the prognostic significance of these variants requires categorization based on their mechanism of genesis and 9q34 deletion status.

profile.name: BCR::ABL1 Fusion
profile.summary: The BCR-ABL fusion protein, commonly referred to as the Philadelphia chromosome, is one of the most studied fusion genes in cancer. It has widely been considered the initiating event in chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). However, despite its ability to initiate disease in mice, its status as an initiating mutation is in dispute. In what is commonly used as the poster-child for targeted therapeutics, the development and use of imatinib in the clinic has led to profound improvements in the prognosis of the disease. However, imatinib resistance is still seen in patients with mutations in the ABL kinase domain of the fusion, most notably the T315I variant. In patients resistant to imatinib, either acquired or otherwise, second generation BCR-ABL TKI's (dasatinib and nilotinib) have seen some success in delivering a tumor response. Third generation ABL1 inhibitor ponatinib is the only FDA approved drug with activity against T315I . However due to risk of life-threatening blood clots and severe narrowing of blood vessels ponatinib is ONLY approved for T315I-positive CML or T315I-positive Ph+ ALL or in cases of CML, Ph+ ALL with resistance or intolerance to other approved ABL1 inhibitors.

evidence.disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence.evidence_statement: A small case series examined molecular features along with clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical characteristics of sarcomas with EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusions. The study included 6 cases (5 males and 1 female; age range 24-67 years), comprising 3 male cases of primary bone tumors of the radius and the remaining 3 cases involving primary soft tissue tumors. A dual-color, EWSR1 break-apart probe set (chr22q12 proximal and distal probes) detected EWSR1 rearrangement and concurrent amplification of its 5'-region in all cases. The EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusion was confirmed using the corresponding FISH probes. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing identified the fusion joining the 5'-end of EWSR1 (exon 7) and 3'-end of NFATC2 (exon 3). Together, the recurrent EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion identified a novel entity of small round cell sarcoma.

evidence.disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence.evidence_statement: This landmark study represents the first description of the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion in Ewing-like sarcomas, leading to the establishment of 'round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions' as a new disease entity in the 2020 WHO Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors. Four male cases (aged 16-39 years) of primary bone tumors were included; all expressed an in-frame EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion transcript. Array-CGH (n=3 cases) and interphase FISH (n=1 case) revealed amplification of chromosomes 22q12 and 20q13. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing revealed fusion between exon 8 of EWSR1 and exon 3 of NFATC2. Using the fiber-FISH technique, the genomic breakpoints were mapped to intron 8 of EWSR1 (22q12) and intron 2 of NFATC2 (20q13). Mechanistically, this fusion results in loss of the N-terminal regulatory region and replacement of a weak nuclear localization signal (NLS) of NFATC2 with a strong NLS of EWSR1, leading to an uncontrolled nuclear localization and activation of the chimera protein.

This study analyzed over 300 patient with advanced solid tumors and melanoma across 22 tumor types from four KEYNOTE clinical trials to define genomic and immune predictors of response to pembrolizumab (anti–PD-1 immunotherapy). Using whole-exome sequencing and NanoString gene profiling, they evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the T cell–inflamed gene expression profile (GEP) in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded pretreatment samples. TMB cut-off values for the pan-tumor and single-indication clinical cohorts were the Youden Index values derived in AUROC analysis (102.5 for pan-cancer, 86 for HNSCC, and 191.5 for melanoma group). TMB and GEP profiles were also analyzed within The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database of 6384 tumors and the WES cut-off >100 mutations per exome was chosen for high TMB to match the Youden TBM pan-cancer cut-offs. TMB and GEP were independently predictive of clinical response and progression-free survival in KEYNOTE cohorts, and together they stratified patients into four biologically distinct subgroups: those with high TMB/high GEP had the highest objective response rates (37–57%), and the longest progression-free survival, whereas those with low TMB/high GEP or high TMB/low GEP showed moderate response rate (12-35% and 11-42%, respectively), and patients with low TMB/low GEP tumors rarely responded (0–9%). The two markers were only weakly correlated (Spearman correlation coefficient at r ~ 0.2), indicating that TMB and GEP are independent predictive markers, with TMB capturing neoantigen load, while GEP reflecting T-cell activation within the tumor microenvironment. Integrative analyses of TCGA data confirmed these findings and revealed resistance-associated alterations such as mutation in STK11, KEAP1, and APC in high TMB and low GEP lung and colorectal cancers, but not in the pan-cancer analysis. In addition, TMB highly correlated with neoantigen load in pan-cancer cohort (r=0.87), HNSCC (r=0.83), and melanoma cohort (r=0.9). Overall, the study established TMB and GEP as complementary, tumor-agnostic predictors of benefit from PD-1 blockade and provided a framework for precision immunotherapy and biomarker-guided combination strategies.

evidence.evidence_statement: In the TIMER dataset, levels of MMP1 is increased in cancers compared with normal tissue, where its levels in sacituzumab govitecan (SG)-resistant tumours are higher than SG-sensitive tumours by IHC. In the TCGA database, high levels of MMP1 is associated with poor prognosis in patients with hormone-positive breast cancer. Breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7 and T47D) slowly exposed to, and eventually becoming resistant to sacituzumab govitecan exhibit mesenchymal-like morphology and increased mRNA expression of MMP1. MMP1 overexpression in SG-resistant breast cancer cell lines is associated with increased colony formation and migration. Mechanistically, MMP1 induces EMT rhough NF-kB pathway activation, while inhibition of MMP1 overcomes SG resistance in pre-clinical models. Together, these evidence shows that MMP1 overexpression is associated with SG resistance.

The Phase 3 trial for the selective and brain-penetrant RET kinase inhibitor selpercatinib in Medullary Thyroid Cancer (MTC) LIBRETTO-531 (NCT04211337) consisted of 291 total patients. The patients had pathologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic MTC, and had no history of treatment with kinase inhibitors. Patients had a prospectively identified pathogenic RET alteration, either somatic or germline, and 182 patients had RET M918T (~63%). From the patients with M918T, 121 were treated with selpercatinib, and 61 were treated with control (physician’s choice of vandetanib or cabozantinib). In the M918T subgroup analysis, control patients had median progression-free survival (PFS) of 17.5 months, while in the selpercatinib-treated patients the median PFS was not met. Hazard Ratio (95% CI) was 0.40 (0.21–0.77) between M918T control and selpercatinib treated patients.

profile.name: RET M918T
profile.summary: RET M918T is the most common somatically acquired mutation in medullary thyroid cancer (MTC). While there currently are no RET-specific inhibiting agents, promiscuous kinase inhibitors have seen some success in treating RET overactivity. Data suggests however, that the M918T mutation may lead to drug resistance, especially against the VEGFR-inhibitor motesanib. It has also been suggested that RET M918T leads to more aggressive MTC with a poorer prognosis.

drug.mechanism: RET inhibitor (also reported to inhibit other kinases including VEGFR1/2/3 and FGFR1/2/3)

evidence.evidence_statement: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled biomarker-selected adjuvant study (ALASCCA, NCT02647099; colorectal carcinoma; n = 626; group A: PIK3CA exon 9/20, n = 314), aspirin 160 mg daily (group A n = 157) for 3 years reduced colorectal cancer recurrence vs placebo (group A n = 157) in the PIK3CA hotspot subgroup (3-yr cumulative incidence 7.7% vs 14.1%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24 - 0.98; P = 0.04) with 3-yr DFS 88.5% vs 81.4% (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.34 - 1.08). Severe AEs occurred in 16.8% vs 11.6% with events including GI bleeding and subarachnoid hemorrhage, and one out of the 4 observed deaths was deemed possibly related to aspirin; OS at 5 yr was not significantly different (91.6% vs 90.1%; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.37 - 1.68).

evidence.evidence_statement: This part of the open-label multipart phase 3 trial, CheckMate 277 (Trial ID: 29658845), examined the performance of nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to chemotherapy among non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with a high tumour mutational burden (TMB) (>= 10 mutations/ megabase). Stage IV/ recurrent NSCLC patients that were chemotherapy treatment naïve were recruited. Patients with tumour programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression of at least 1% were randomly assigned to receive nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab monotherapy, or chemotherapy; while those with tumour PD-L1 expression of < 1% were randomly assigned to be treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab plus chemotherapy, or chemotherapy. Tissue TMB was determined by the FoundationOne CDx assay. Patients with high TMB achieved significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n = 139) (1-year PFS of 42%, median PFS of 7.2 months with 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.5 to 13.2), compared to chemotherapy alone (n = 160) (1-year PFS of 13.2%, median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.4 to 5.8) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 97.5% CI, 0.41 to 0.81; P<0.001). 45.3% of patients achieved objective response with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, compared to 26.9% with chemotherapy. The benefit of nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy was consistent across histologic subtypes and despite whether the tumour PD-L1 expression was at least 1% or lower than 1%. On the contrary, among the patients with low TMB, the clinical benefit was not significantly different between patients treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n= 191) (median PFS of 3.2 months with 95% CI, 2.7 to 4.3) and those treated with chemotherapy (n=189) (median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.3 to 5.6) (HR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.35). In conclusion, this study demonstrated significant clinical benefit of first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy among NSCLC patients with a high TMB, irrespective of the expression level of tumour PD-L1.

evidence.evidence_statement: In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%. Across the 200 mg-random and 300 mg-random cohorts, the 770_SVD subtype represented 24.7% and 18.0% of patients, with cORRs of 47.6% and 56.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, the 769_ASV subtype accounted for 21.2% and 23.6%, with cORRs of 33.3% and 57.1%, respectively. Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

evidence.evidence_statement: In a retrospective LUAD cohort treated with PD-1 plus CTLA-4 blockade (n = 59; LRP1B-MT n = 15, LRP1B-WT n = 44), LRP1B-mutated tumors showed significantly longer PFS (log-rank p = 0.0016), along with higher rates of DCB (p = 0.03) and improved best overall response (p = 0.02) compared with LRP1B-WT tumors. In the TCGA-LUAD cohort without immunotherapy (n = 507), PFS (p = 0.43) and OS (p = 0.16) did not differ by LRP1B status, indicating the survival advantage was specific to ICI treatment.

In this study the authors examined six gynecologic tract perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) that were previously diagnosed as PEComa but demonstrated unusual morphology suggestive of TFE3 involvement. A comparison group of eleven conventional PEComas was also included. TFE3 break-apart FISH and immunohistochemistry were utilized to evaluate for TFE3 gene abnormalities. TFE3 rearrangements were identified in all six test cases, whereas none of the conventional PEComas showed TFE3 rearrangement. The TFE3-rearranged tumors showed a distinctive immunophenotype characterized by strong nuclear TFE3 expression, absent or minimal melanocytic marker expression, and lack of smooth muscle marker positivity, in contrast to the conventional PEComa profile. Morphologically, TFE3-rearranged PEComas demonstrated predominantly pure epithelioid clear-cell morphology with an alveolar or nested growth pattern, differing from the mixed epithelioid–spindled architecture typical of conventional lesions. The cohort included five females and one male, aged 17–52 years. The authors concluded that they have identified a distinct subset of PEComas with characteristic morphology and immunophenotype, defined by v::TFE3 gene fusions, which separate them diagnostically from conventional PEComa and support their classification within the family of TFE3-associated neoplasms.

In this 2025 study, the authors included 14 confirmed TFE3-rearranged perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas), previously classified as benign (9 tumors) or malignant (5 tumors), and compared them to the molecular features of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. DNA sequencing and FISH were utilized to investigate genetic correlates of malignancy. Complex chromosomal copy number alterations (CNAs) were detected in three of four (75%) assessable malignant tumors and were absent in all benign tumors. Inactivating alterations in TP53, RB1, or ATRX were rare among the malignant tumors, observed in only 1 of 5 cases, contrasting with patterns seen in malignant TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. The cohort comprised 11 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, from 9 to 64 years (median 31.5 years). Tumors occurred in diverse anatomical sites, including the uterus, extremities, colon, nasal cavity, neck, retroperitoneum, bladder, and ovary. The authors concluded that complex CNAs are a frequent genetic correlate of malignancy in TFE3-rearranged PEComas and may serve as a diagnostic marker, and that these tumors lack the highly recurrent TP53, RB1, or ATRX alterations characteristic of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas.

evidence.disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence.evidence_statement: This case series presented 7 NFATC2-rearranged sarcomas, including 4 EWSR1::NFATC2 and 3 FUS::NFATC2 cases, and developed an ACAN-encoding aggrecan immunohistochemistry as a diagnostic tool for these tumors. All cases were primary bone tumors with 6 located in the long bones (4 femur, 2 tibia) and 1 in the ilium. Using RNA-seq, the FUS::NFATC2 fusion was found to join exon 6 of FUS with exon 3 of NFATC2 in all three cases. FISH analysis using the FUS break-apart probe (BAP) was applied to one case and identified an unbalanced pattern with gains of the 5’ FISH probe (data not shown). Array-CGH further showed more complex genomic profiles in all FUS::NFATC2 cases compared with one tested EWSR1::NFATC2 sample. This study expanded the evidence for the recurrent FUS::NFATC2 fusion in the rare round cell sarcoma.

evidence.disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence.evidence_statement: This is the first study to identify the FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion. Using multi-omics approach and targeted sequencing, the authors comprehensively characterized the molecular landscape of a large cohort of Ewing sarcoma (-like) tumors (101 samples, including 65 tumors and 36 cell lines). Seven of 62 (11.3%) tumors analyzed by RNA-seq were found to lack a typical Ewing sarcoma EWSR1 gene fusion. One case was found to harbor a novel, in-frame FUS::NFATC2 fusion joining the TET family member FUS (exon 6) and the non-ETS family transcription factor NFATC2 (exon 9). This observation was further verified by RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing. This work provided the first evidence of FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion, which leads to the establishment of the new disease entity “round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions”.

In a pooled analysis of five phase I–II trials and an expanded access program of ONC201 (dordaviprone) for recurrent H3 K27M–mutant diffuse midline glioma (NCT02525692, NCT03295396, NCT03416530, NCT03134131, NCT05392374; n = 50), the RANO-HGG ORR was 20.0% (1 CR, 9 PR; 95% CI 10.0–33.7) with DCR 40.0% (95% CI 26.4–54.8; SD n = 10), median DOR 11.2 months (95% CI 3.8–NR), TTR 8.3 months (range 1.9–15.9), 6-month PFS 35.1% (95% CI 21.2–49.3), and median OS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.0–20.3), with 12- and 24-month OS of 57.3% (95% CI 41.4–70.3) and 34.7% (95% CI 20.7–49.2). Using RANO-LGG criteria, the ORR was 26.0% (95% CI 14.6–40.3; 6 PR, 7 MR) and DCR 42.0% (95% CI, 28.2 to 56.8; SD, n = 8), and when combining the best responses across either RANO system, the ORR was 30.0% (95% CI 17.9–44.6) and DCR 44.0% (95% CI, 30.0–58.7; SD, n = 7); corticosteroid reduction ≥50% occurred in 46.7% of evaluable patients (7/15; 95% CI, 21.3–73.4), median TTR 3.7 months (range 1.9–5.6) and KPS/LPS improvement in 20.6% (7/34, 95% CI, 8.7 to 37.9) median TTR 3.5 months (range 1.9–22.4).

In this 2025 retrospective study, 14 spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) cases previously identified as possessing ZFP64::NCOA2 or ZFP64::NCOA3 fusions were pulled from clinical archives to assess clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular genetic features. Key observations include a strong male prevalence, middle-age occurrence (median 41 years; range 22-81 years), wide anatomic distribution, and NCOA3 fusions are more common than NCOA2 fusions. Arising primarily from soft tissue, these tumors displayed both fascicular and spindle cell morphologies within a hyalinized collagenous background and various degrees of skeletal muscle marker expression, although occasional focal or diffuse round cell morphologies were also observed. All cases were analyzed by targeted RNA sequencing platforms from various laboratories, with specific fusions noted between ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA2 exon 14 fusion in 6 cases (43%) and ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA3 exon 14/15 fusion in 8 cases (57%). Ten of these cases were also characterized by DNA methylation profiling, revealing ZFP64 SCRMS as an epigenetic sarcoma subtype distinct from other RMS. SCRMS with ZFP64::NCOA2/3 fusions are associated with frequent distant metastases, local recurrences, and death, and therefore these fusions may provide benefit as prognostic markers.

In the phase 1/2 trial LIBRETTO-121 (NCT03899792), for patients 0.5-21 yrs old with advanced RET-altered solid tumors, dosing started at 92 mg/m2 twice a day of Selpercatinib. Patients had RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 14), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (PTC, n = 10), or other tumors (n = 3). M918T was the most common mutation in MTC (10/14) and NCOA4-RET fusion most common in PTC (5/10). Treatment ranged from 0.4 to 40.8 months, and 22 pts remained on treatment at time of this report. Overall response rate was 10/12 in patients with measurable disease at baseline, with 1 having stable disease and 1 with progressive disease. No PTC or MTC patients had progressive disease. At median follow up of 18 months, the median progression free survival had not yet been reached.
